seed_policy: One seed, frozen here. Generation uses only this seed. If a gate fails, fix the rules or the process parameters and record why; never try other seeds until one passes. power_sim may scan neighbouring seeds to report variance, never to choose the generation seed.
description: Planted rules of the labelled synthetic layer over CRMArena-Pro deals (WP32, HAR-131; spec docs/data/synthetic-layer-v1.md). Deal outcomes are drawn from these rules plus noise, so a learner that recovers them from previous deals proves the loop recovers planted rules. It does not prove the rules hold in real selling. Bench-only: never read by the platform, never shown to the agent, the evals or the knowledge store.

scoring.description: The A/B/C knowledge-uplift experiment and every claim that the loop recovers planted rules are scored on the hidden_company_specific group only. eval_known rules are already encoded by HAR-97 evals or seeded knowledge, so they measure the generator loop (the evals catch violations and revision fixes them), not learning from outcomes. control rules are nulls.

outcome.description: Forward in time (forward.py). Running health h(t) = sum of log_odds of the rules holding so far (an exception counts only with the rule it modifies). Each day: stage advance hazard and synthetic reply odds rise with h(t); an exit hazard exit_base_daily * exp(-exit_health_slope * h(t)) can put the deal dormant (no more advances or synthetic replies; it closes lost at its CloseDate). A deal that stays active closes at its CloseDate won with probability sigmoid(base_log_odds + h(close) + u_account), u_account ~ Normal(0, account_effect_sd) drawn once per account and never written. No record dated before the close depends on the outcome draw.

learnability_gates.basis: power_sweep.py runs the forward kernel (power_sim.py) on the stand-in world (world.py) with the WP31 profile mixes (base_profile.v1.json), time split 67/33 by close date, over sweep_seeds seeds from the frozen seed, in two modes: clean (gated) and noisy (extraction error per observation class, current deals seen at a decision time; reported). Numbers, the seed pass rate and every failing seed are in bench/reports/synthetic-power-v1.json, pinned to this file's content hash.

gate_exceptions.reason: 34/40 seeds pass; the 6 misses each fail one gate by a small margin (null 0.031/0.030; hidden-only AUC 0.726/0.744; cc-presence 0.032/0.034). The user accepted this after the final lead-approved calibration round; no further rounds. Only this exact failure is waived: any other sweep failure still blocks generation.

failures: syn1_written_handover_exempts sign recovered in 0.78 of seeds < 0.8
syn1_quote_before_economic_buyer sign recovered in 0.03 of seeds < 0.8
syn1_requested_pause_ignored sign recovered in 0.45 of seeds < 0.8
gate_exceptions.reason: Real-base sweep (power_sweep --base, clean): 23 of 40 seeds fail at least one per-seed gate (28 misses): oracle AUC below 0.65 in 17 seeds, learner AUC in 6, cc_incremental_auc in 3, win rate in 1, and one wrong hidden-rule sign (syn1_second_quote_within_30d) in 1 seed. The clean seed pass rate is 0.425 (noisy 0.075, reported and never gated). Separately, the sweep-level sign recovery of three eval-known rules misses the 0.80 gate: quote_before_economic_buyer 0.03 (real prevalence 0.72, nearly collinear with the intercept), requested_pause_ignored 0.45, written_handover_exempts 0.78. Eval-known sign recovery is NOT a per-seed gate, so these three rules do NOT cause the 23 failing seeds. The user approved this exception, and re-confirmed it with these true reasons on 2026-10-03: eval-known rules are never used for learning claims, only the 4 hidden rules are. The waiver therefore also absorbs, inside the 0.425 pass rate, one per-seed hidden-sign failure and three per-seed cc failures. Hidden-rule sign gates, the null and cc gates (sweep mean) and every other failure still block generation at sweep level; no threshold is lowered.

power_sim_noise.description: Noisy power-simulation mode (power_sim.observe): each planted feature is observed through the platform's extraction for its class, with a miss rate and a false-positive rate; current deals are seen at a decision time inside the deal (a uniform share of the window), not at the close.

crm_explicit.basis: CRM field and stage events are deterministic rules (claims standing crm_explicit); 2% covers late or missing CRM writes (assumed).

identity_title.basis: Sender-to-contact resolution plus title parsing; assumed 10% miss, 2% wrong function.

llm_extraction.basis: 1 - fact_recall 0.805 of the live extraction benchmark (bench/reports/live-extract-2026-10-02-v4.md); false positives assumed 3%.

rules.statement: In an account whose relationship owner changed in a reorganisation, advancing the opportunity to Quote or Negotiation or sending pricing before a new owner has held the role for 14 days, or while that owner is acting or interim, lowers the win odds.
rules.feature: exists commercial step s (stage to Quote/Negotiation, or a pricing outbound) with t_reorg < t_s and NOT (champion named after t_reorg, held >= owner_stable_min_days at t_s, title not acting/interim at t_s)
realized_by: E1/E2 champion leaves or changes role

rules.statement: When the deal's champion leaves the company or moves to a role away from the deal and nobody takes over that role within 30 days, the win odds fall.
rules.feature: champion departure or away-move at t_d and no champion named in (t_d, t_d + replacement_window_days]

rules.statement: When a new buyer-side person joins the deal, seller outreach to that person within 14 days that also includes the champion raises the win odds.
rules.feature: new buyer-side contact enters at t_e; first seller outbound or meeting to that contact in (t_e, t_e + 14d] has the champion among recipients

rules.statement: When a new buyer-side person joins the deal, seller outreach to that person within 14 days that leaves the champion out lowers the win odds.
rules.feature: new buyer-side contact enters at t_e; first seller outbound or meeting to that contact in (t_e, t_e + 14d] omits the champion

rules.statement: If the champion handed the deal over in writing before the new person was contacted, leaving the champion out has no effect on the win odds.
rules.feature: a first-party message from the champion delegating the deal to the entrant precedes the first outbound to the entrant
realized_by: E7 written handover by the champion

rules.statement: Reaching the Quote stage before the economic buyer has replied to the seller or met with the seller lowers the win odds.
rules.feature: t_stage(Quote) < first reply or meeting attendance by the economic buyer (or the buyer never engages before Quote)

rules.statement: Having at least three different buyer-side people reply to the seller or attend a meeting before the Quote stage raises the win odds.
rules.feature: count of distinct buyer contacts with a reply or attendance before t_stage(Quote) >= 3

rules.statement: When the buyer asks for time until a stated date and the seller writes to the buyer again before that date, the win odds fall.
rules.feature: a timing-request reply names date D at t_r; a seller outbound to the same account falls in (t_r, D)

rules.statement: At this company, deals where the seller writes to someone with an operations job title before sending a quote are won more often.
rules.feature: a seller email (base or synthetic) whose recipients include an operations-title contact, dated before the OpportunityStageChanged to Quote
realized_by: S2 synthetic seller note to an operations contact (ops_note_share)

decision.changes: recipients and next action before Quote: whether to write to an operations-title contact
decision.scored_by: hidden-only planted value of the chosen action on the same deal snapshot for every arm (spec d2): regret = best available hidden value minus chosen value; uplift = regret(A) - regret(B)

audit.why_not_encoded: judges whether the right people are involved for one action (champion, security, executives); it never prefers an operations role and has no notion of before-quote timing or of outcome odds
buyer-side breadth and threading for the stage; the job function of a recipient is not an input
names pricing before technical validation; it says nothing about an operations contact
keeps the champion involved when a stakeholder enters; no function or before-quote condition

gold fails copying a Supply Chain Coordinator and an Operations Assistant (buyer-side, not verified in the buying group) onto a pricing reply as OVER_THREADED; it penalises unverified breadth on a pricing thread, not a seller writing to an operations contact before the quote. It is a revision risk for P1, so P1 is scored on the decision BEFORE eval-driven revision (spec d2)
include the person the buyer asks to include: triggered by a buyer request, with no operations or before-quote condition

rules.statement: At this company, when the buyer pushes back on price after the quote, changing the quoted amount loses more often than keeping it and explaining the value.
rules.feature: after a buyer price objection dated at or after the Quote stage, a CRMFieldChanged on Opportunity.Amount by the seller (the hold arm is a seller value email with the amount unchanged)
realized_by: X2 buyer price objection at Quote (pushback_at_quote_share, never near a real customer email)
X3 seller choice: amount edit (reprice_share) or value email

decision.changes: CTA / commercial step at Quote after a price objection: re-price (CRM update) or hold and make the value case
decision.scored_by: hidden-only planted value of the chosen action on the same deal snapshot for every arm (spec d2): regret = best available hidden value minus chosen value; uplift = regret(A) - regret(B)

audit.why_not_encoded: deterministic: numbers in a draft must be supported by source evidence (no invented discount); a re-price recorded in the CRM is supported, so the eval never judges whether re-pricing or holding is the better move
the size of the ask relative to the relationship; it has no price-concession or hold-the-price condition
value claims must match the customer's pain; it never compares holding the price with changing it, and never blocks
maps the approval path when the economic buyer is unknown; no pricing condition
answer a cost question in writing before proposing a call: about the channel and order of an answer, never about re-pricing versus holding the price after an objection

rules.statement: At this company, when the seller first answers a buyer who has a technical job title, copying a second person from the seller's own team wins more often.
rules.feature: the first seller email answering a technical-title buyer carries a second seller-domain address in cc
realized_by: X4 seller reply to the first technical-title buyer email (always), cc decision cc_colleague_share

decision.changes: recipients (internal cc) on the first reply to a technical-title buyer
decision.scored_by: hidden-only planted value of the chosen action on the same deal snapshot for every arm (spec d2): regret = best available hidden value minus chosen value; uplift = regret(A) - regret(B)

audit.why_not_encoded: deterministic: recipients exist and belong to the account or our org; a seller colleague is allowed, and whether adding one helps is out of scope

buyer-side breadth (UNDER/OVER_THREADED); seller-side people are not counted. The two eval cases that cc a solutions engineer treat it as neutral: over_threading/acme_cp4 fails on the exec call and user cc and says the engineer alone would be fine; correct_timing/beta_cp2 passes on other grounds
security documents before a review meeting; no internal-cc condition

judges channel and audience fit; one recorded judge note (cassettes/judges, PR #20) calls an internal cc 'appropriate for customer-facing content'. That is channel suitability, never a reason to cc or a better score for it, and says nothing about win odds

the three copied people are buyer-side staff, not seller colleagues, on a pricing reply; it penalises breadth and never judges one seller colleague on the reply to a technical buyer. A judge applying it loosely could strip P3's cc, so P3 is scored before revision (spec d2)
include the person the buyer asks to include: a buyer-side request, not an internal cc

rules.statement: At this company, sending a second quote to the same customer within thirty days of another quote that is still open loses more often.
rules.feature: at the Quote stage change, another quote to the same account was opened in the previous 30 days (a REAL base quote of another opportunity, or a synthetic Quote entry of an earlier deal), and the seller sends a separate quote (the alternative is folding it into the open one)
realized_by: S3 the account's other quotes: real base Quote records (0.60 per opportunity) and earlier synthetic Quote entries
X5 seller choice: separate quote (separate_quote_share) or fold

decision.changes: CRM update / next action at Quote: send a separate quote or fold it into the open one
decision.scored_by: hidden-only planted value of the chosen action on the same deal snapshot for every arm (spec d2): regret = best available hidden value minus chosen value; uplift = regret(A) - regret(B)

audit.why_not_encoded: deterministic: the same email, meeting or CRM action was not already done; a separate quote for another opportunity is a different action, so it is never flagged
no urgency after a concern and no repeated nudges; it never counts open quotes, and never blocks
a light check-in after silence; no quote condition

rules.statement: The industry of the account has no effect at all on the win odds of its deals.
The amount band of the opportunity has no effect at all on its win odds.
Which seller owns the opportunity has no effect at all on its win odds.
How many outbound emails the seller sent on the deal has no direct effect on its win odds; any link runs through the planted rules.
rules.feature: count of base outbound EmailMessage records on the opportunity

rules.statement: The weekday of the first outbound email on the deal has no effect at all on its win odds.
rules.feature: weekday of the first base outbound EmailMessage

rules.statement: A new executive who joins the account outside the deal's buying group has no effect at all on the win odds.
rules.feature: E4 new executive event whose function is not in the deal's buying group

rules.statement: Another opportunity opened on the same account in the thirty days before this one has no effect at all on the win odds.
rules.feature: base data: another Opportunity on the same Account has a CreatedDate in the 30 days before this one's CreatedDate
